outcome.technical: R70: tools/check-browser-install.py now holds its promise in two independent halves. (1) By reading: run_script calls script_problems before starting any step and never runs a script the reader refuses, and new case sd8 reports the same reading for the steps the cases run. The reader is a new section, a subset shell lexer/parser that refuses any shape it does not read. Its rule is positive: every command word is a bare literal name that is a stub, a shell stub, an ALLOWED_TOOLS entry, a function the script defines, or a builtin on the new BUILTINS table, called in the shape its row allows (set only as `set --`, printf only with a single-quoted format, eval only of the apt-config stub's output, `[` only with -z/-n/-d or =/!= on double-quoted operands). Only lowercase names may be assigned, no assignment may come before a command, and a redirection may go only to /dev/null, "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" or >&1/>&2. Arithmetic, subscripts, ${x@P}, ${!x}, process substitution, backquotes, here-docs, & and subshells are refused. sd7 (absolute paths) is part of the gate. (2) By construction: _prelude makes every variable of the step's environment read-only (PATH and the stubs' variables among them), unsets BASH_CMDS and BASH_ALIASES and makes them read-only, makes the not-found handler read-only, and disables every builtin not on BUILTINS with `enable -n`, enable last. How each R70 escape is held (reader row / construction row): command -p (bx6 / bk1), relative-path command word (bx7 / reader only), variable-built command word (bx8 / reader only), exec (bx9 / bk3), PATH= (bx10 / bk5, bk6), env, hash -p, enable -f, source, ., builtin, trap (bp10 / bk4, bk7, bk8, bk9, bk2, bk10). Escapes found beyond the reviewer's list: eval of runtime text (bx12), printf -v through an array subscript (bx13), [ -v (bp10), a redirection to a variable-built host path (bx11), BASH_CMDS (bk11), STUB_BIN= (bk12). The docstring's 'stays outside' list now names: the reader is not bash, the node vm harness, what tools and stubs can read, STEP_TIMEOUT not ending every process, and bash 3.2's not-found channel. Existing rows: bx1 and bx5 now reach outside by paths the reader cannot see, so they still test the sudo stub and the node harness; every bx row names the half that must refuse it; bm4 now uses `[ -n "" ]` instead of the disabled `false`. New selftest cases: bp9, bp10, bp11, bx6-bx13, bk1-bk12; selftest 87/87. tools/gate-parity.py: AUDITED_EXEMPTIONS row BUILTINS -> bp9 (before the row was added, gate-parity was red on the unaudited table). R71: the only copy of the sentence (git grep 'seed that saves': ci.yml:414) now reads 'a failed seed that still saves an entry (the seed that saved, run 44426388905 above, had installed)', resting on that comment's own record of the run. action.yml's header comment and CONTRIBUTING.md's install-check paragraph describe the reader and the construction. CI run 44671682900, on a probe commit of these five files: green on every job. The lint job printed `browser install: 28 of 28 cases held`, with no 'could not run here' in the log. selftests (linux, plain 1) and (linux, stress 1) each printed `tools/check-browser-install.py 87 cases` ok, so all 87 cases hold on ubuntu's bash 5. selftests (windows, plain 1) and (windows, cp1252 3) each printed `20 cases` ok. On Windows the posix-only half does not run: 68 cases (bi1-bi10, sp1-sp6, sk1-sk4, bm1-bm23, bx1-bx13, bk1-bk12) are replaced by one recorded skip line, bc0, which names the host problem. What runs there is bp1-bp11 plus sd1-sd8. The file's total does not tell skips apart, a known harness limit already recorded as a finding. Gates, each run on its own: check 28/28 (exit 0); gate-parity exit 0; gate-parity --selftest 135/135; the task gate as one command, exit 0 (2/2 files ok, 222 cases); check-rendered-artifacts --before-commit, check-example-ledgers, check-git-pipeline and measure-context --gate each exit 0; ruff 'All checks passed!'; vermin exit 0; the full sweep after the last edit, exit 0 with 198/198 files ok and 19739 cases. The narrow sweep's first run caught pn0 in test__output_lints on my own `stack[-1] == "case"` (read as a count); I fixed it with _innermost() and test__output_lints passed 183/183 when rerun alone. CPU time of the check (user+sys, /usr/bin/time -p), each measured twice with a gap: before 6.04 s and 7.23 s; after 6.34 s and 6.26 s, so the change is within the spread. The reader costs 1.05 ms CPU per pass over the four steps (measured once).
